newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on cold weather forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on cold weather forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, boosted by Midwest and Northeast forecasts for some of the coldest air of the season later this week, industry sources said.
February climbed 13.9 cents to close at $3.393 per million British thermal units. March settled 13.6 cents higher at $2.996. Most others ended steady to up 11.9 cents.

"Some forecasters changed their minds about the warming trend next week and caught some people short," said one Midwest trader, adding it will take some sustained cold to support prices near current levels.

But despite the approach of more Arctic air this week, traders noted there was little conviction about market direction, particularly with concerns about rising stocks partly offsetting bullish weather forecasts.

Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report range widely from 40 to 150 bcf versus a draw of 197 for the same week last year. East Coast stocks, which already are 20 percent over last year, fell by 127 bcf in 1996, meaning the eastern surplus is likely to grow further in next report.

Technical traders said February has been stuck in a range for the last week or so, with support still seen in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.185 and better buying likely in the $2.60s. Resistance was pegged around $3.60, then in the $3.80-3.84 area and then at $3.96.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained about five cents Tuesday to about the $4.00 level. Midcon pipes slipped five to 10 cents to $4.30 or lower. New York city gate gas prices slipped more than a quarter to about the $4.30 level.

Separately, Tenneco said cold weather in the U.S. Gulf forced producers to cut 300-400 mmcfd of natgas from its seven bcfd system, but most of the shut in gas was expected back later today or tomorrow.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose six cents to $2.456. NYMEX said an estimated 38,052 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 34,461.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, February closed up 17 cents at $3.23, while deferred months finished two to 16 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.1 cents to 16.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 82 contracts traded, down from Monday's total of 215.
